clue.text: Turned incognito after role, essentially avoided identification

indicators.note: after places the rearranged incognito behind what is left of role
the essential, central letters of the word role are left out, keeping only its ends
turned here means twisted round into a new order, so the letters of incognito are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone went incognito after a role, cleverly avoiding being identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially avoided' drops the centre of ROLE, not the whole word; 'Turned' gives COGNITION, and the clue's 'incognito' surface hides that the anagram is nearly the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Recognising someone is identifying them, so recognition is a synonym for identification.

clue.text: Mausoleum feature is yet undecided

definitions.meaning: a mausoleum may keep a body or relics on show: remains that are there to be seen
the idiom said of an outcome nobody knows yet

explanation.surface: A tour guide is unsure about some feature of a mausoleum.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal and punning: in a mausoleum the remains are what visitors come to view.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the outcome is still unknown; read literally it describes bodily remains on display in a tomb.

clue.text: Missing the odd school disco is a pain

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of school and disco keeps only their even letters

explanation.surface: A school disco that is missing some odd element turns out to be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing the odd' keeps the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters: COL from school and IC from disco.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is a severe abdominal pain, often in babies, so it is an example of a pain.

clue.text: Police try to bury dodgy tapes

indicators.note: burying something puts it inside, so the try word encloses the jumbled letters

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, signalling the letters of tapes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police attempt to hide some incriminating tapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is a noun here, as in 'have a go', not a courtroom verb, though the police surface pushes the trial reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police force of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: Philistine, a broadcaster with the university? Unbelievable!

parts.note: Philistine is the setter of this puzzle, who refers to himself as I
Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A boorish person working for a broadcaster and a university? Incredible!
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym Philistine also means an uncultured person, which is what the surface pretends it is. SKY is a UK satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: I ask you! is an exclamation of exasperated disbelief, matching an outraged cry of incredulity.

clue.text: Broke in and disturbed Rupert (it's in the papers)

indicators.note: the jumbled name is said to be in the papers, so the papers word goes round it

parts.note: identity papers are ID

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of Rupert are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone broke in and upset Rupert, and the story made the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's in the papers' reads as press gossip, perhaps about Rupert Murdoch, but 'papers' means identity papers. 'disturbed' gives RRUPTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force one's way into a place, so irrupted means broke in.

clue.text: Detectives finding information on bed with rope around its end

indicators.note: on is a down-clue placing: the information word sits on top of the rest

parts.note: news is information
a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: around means the rope word wraps round the single end letter

parts.note: a lanyard is a short cord or rope
its refers back to bed; the end of bed is D

explanation.surface: Detectives track down information found on a bed with a rope looped round its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts D, the last letter of bed, inside LANYARD to give LANDYARD.
explanation.definitionFit: New Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, used by metonymy for its detectives.

clue.text: Lacking 19 1 across possibly, apropos the rise of first-rate aria

definitions.note: the condition of lacking face recognition, a noun phrase naming the disorder

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of apropos might be arranged some other way
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
an aria is a song

explanation.surface: A rather random remark about a top-class aria rising, apropos of lacking recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 and 1 across are FACE and RECOGNITION. 'possibly' rearranges APROPOS into PROSOPA, and 'the rise of' turns AISONG into GNOSIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosopagnosia is face blindness, the neurological inability to recognise people's faces.

clue.text: Pure red tea stirred by a French man or woman

parts.note: un is French for a
an adult is a grown man or woman

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of red tea are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pure red tea, stirred by a Frenchman or woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French' gives the French article, not a nationality; 'stirred' rearranges RED TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadulterated means not mixed with anything else, so it is a synonym for pure.

clue.text: City developer rebuilt our slum

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together again differently, so the letters of our slum are rearranged

explanation.surface: An urban developer redeveloped our slum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges OURSLUM into ROMULUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus is the legendary founder of Rome, so he is the developer of a city.

clue.text: This will shed light on gang engaged in crime

definitions.note: a description of the thing, standing for the answer as a noun: a light bulb

indicators.note: the gang is engaged in, that is held within, the crime word

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, loosely a crime
a crew is a gang

explanation.surface: An informant will expose a gang involved in a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: A screw-in is a light bulb with a threaded base, as opposed to a bayonet fitting, so 'shed light on' is meant literally, not as 'reveal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-in bulb gives out light, so it is something that sheds light.

clue.text: Fancy ritzy cars like those in lockdown?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, so the letters of ritzy cars are reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: People stuck in lockdown dream of fancy, glitzy cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges RITZYCARS into STIRCRAZY. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-crazy means driven mad by confinement, as people shut indoors during lockdown can become.

clue.text: Took steps to depose king in full

indicators.note: deposing a king removes him, so the king letter is taken out

parts.note: packed means full
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone took steps to remove a king from power completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to depose' removes K from PACKED to leave PACED.
explanation.definitionFit: Paced means walked with measured steps, so it means took steps.

clue.text: Stop weirdo letters

indicators.note: weirdo suggests something odd, so the letters of stop are scrambled into a strange order

explanation.surface: An order to some oddball to stop sending letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weirdo' rearranges STOP into POST.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is mail, the letters and parcels delivered.

clue.text: Second Greek character, intellectual and imposing

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
mental means relating to the intellect

explanation.surface: A Greek figure who is both intellectual and impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is informal for a moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monumental means huge and impressive, so it is a synonym for imposing.

clue.text: Short and sweet, not worth changing, so approved

indicators.note: not tells you that the letters of worth are to be removed from the fodder
changing means the remaining letters of short and sweet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kept short and sweet: no point altering it, so it was signed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W, O, R, T, H from SHORTANDSWEET to leave SANDSEET, and 'changing' rearranges those into ASSENTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree to something, so assented means approved.

clue.text: Here is game with drunken groom about to wake up

definitions.note: a description of a place, standing for the answer as a noun: where game birds live

indicators.note: about means the jumbled groom goes round the waking word
drunken means unsteady, so the letters of groom are reeled into a new order

parts.note: to rouse is to wake up

explanation.surface: A drunk groom is about to come round after his wedding party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' gives GMOOR, split round the inner piece. A grouse moor is British upland heather where grouse are shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse moor is moorland kept for grouse, the game birds, so it is a place where game is found.

clue.text: Then slowly rue friend welcoming Harry's clue?

definitions.note: the second half of the proverb, repent at leisure, standing for the first half

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the friend word encloses the rest

parts.note: a mate is a friend
a clue for the word HARRYS could read RRY in HAS, which is written out as the letters RRYINHAS

explanation.surface: A friend greets someone, perhaps Harry, with a hint about future regret.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Marry in haste, repent at leisure'. The inner string is itself a clue for HARRY'S: RRY put in HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that a hasty wedding is followed by regret at leisure, so the clue's first words complete its saying.

clue.text: Perhaps Sue overworks

indicators.note: perhaps suggests another possible version, so the letters of sue over are rearranged

explanation.surface: Maybe Sue works too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides at the end of 'overworks': 'Perhaps' rearranges SUEOVER into OEUVRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeuvres are an artist's bodies of work, so the word is a synonym for works.

clue.text: Confront what's been kept under cover during pandemic

definitions.text: what's been kept under cover during pandemic
definitions.meaning: the part of the body covered by masks during the Covid pandemic

explanation.surface: Tackle what has been kept hidden during the pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading points to face masks worn in the Covid pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing an issue is confronting it, and the face is what a mask covers.

clue.text: Middle of Viennese bonbons, round and plump

indicators.note: round means turned round, so the picked letters are read backwards
the middle of the phrase holds a run of letters that straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A Viennese sweet with a round, plump centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' picks ESEBO from vienNESE BONbons and 'round' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, a stronger synonym for plump.

clue.text: Aide could provide estimate

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says to rough up, that is rearrange, the word idea, which gives aide

explanation.surface: An assistant could supply a ballpark figure.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer works as an anagram instruction, with ROUGH as the indicator and IDEA as the fodder, giving AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough idea is an approximate notion of something, which is what an estimate is.

clue.text: See 17
In a clumsy way, one gets plenty wrong

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: wrong means mistaken or out of place, so the letters of plenty are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy gets many things wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges PLENTY into NEPTLY; 'gets' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptly means without skill, which is doing something in a clumsy way.

clue.text: Change a sphere into a cube?

definitions.text: Change a sphere into a cube?

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of a sphere are given a new order

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: turn a ball into a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges ASPHERE into RESHAPE; the whole clue also describes reshaping a sphere into a cube.
explanation.definitionFit: To reshape is to give something a new form, as turning a sphere into a cube would.

clue.text: Agree with boss to go after desktop when nobody's around

indicators.note: to go after places the boss word behind the rest
around says the nobody word goes round the desk letter

parts.note: nobody's means no one's
the top letter of desk is D
a head is a boss

explanation.surface: Office worker agrees with the boss and then heads for the desk when nobody is about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desktop' is one word but splits as desk + top, giving its first letter; 'nobody's' becomes NO ONE'S, apostrophe included in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding one's head is the gesture of saying yes, so it means agree.
